Platform deliverable, GPL-3.0, approved by Garrett 2026-09-14 as a separate executable (own package and process; never linked into proprietary or native estate libraries). Built from the acquired AWCC tree; its six FetchContent dependencies (loguru, json, glfw, imgui, libusb-cmake, stb) are acquired, pinned and compiled into the executable (SYMON_DEP_TREES); system libraries (GL dispatch libglvnd, X11, libudev) are oe-core's, dynamically linked. Run-time boundary: the acpi_call kernel module is required and not yet acquired.

System library from oe-core (libevdev 1.13.7), built as shared AND static in the Platform estate build (EXTRA_OEMESON -Ddefault_library=both) because AWCC's CMake consumes a static libevdev.a through an ExternalProject the estate replaces with the sysroot copy (recipe-level ExternalProject.cmake shadow). Statically linked into awcc; same class as libX11 / libglvnd / libudev (OE-provided system libraries), recorded because it ships inside the executable.

pending_collisions.evidence: ggml will exist three times once Diffuse is acquired: llama.cpp (LLM, ggml-org upstream), whisper.cpp (Diffuse, ggml-org upstream), and stable-diffusion.cpp (Diffuse, leejet/ggml - a PERSONAL FORK). Two upstreams, three copies. Recorded before acquiring, per A3.
pending_collisions.resolution_2026_09_13: libggml is built once from canonical ggml-org/ggml at the commit the pinned llama.cpp syncs (scripts/sync-ggml.last); the vendored llama.cpp/ggml/ was proven byte-identical to it, so llama.cpp consumes libggml via LLAMA_USE_SYSTEM_GGML=ON - one ggml copy for LLM. whisper.cpp and stable-diffusion.cpp (Diffuse, not yet acquired) carry their OWN sync commits/fork; when Diffuse is acquired each must be checked against this tree and either match it or be recorded as a second, distinct ggml identity. The cross-runtime collision is therefore narrowed, not closed.
